2.12 Heart Rate Monitor (Chart)

Displaying a real-time PPG waveform chart and heart rate using LVGL’s chart widget.

Overview

This project creates a medical-style heart rate monitor. The MAX30102 sensor’s raw infrared data is plotted as a scrolling line chart, while computed BPM is displayed in a large text label.

What You’ll Learn

  • Using the LVGL chart widget (lv_chart)

  • Adding data series and scrolling line graphs

  • Real-time data visualization

  • Combining sensor data with dynamic UI updates

How the Code Works

Chart Initialization

A line chart with 90 data points is created to display the PPG (photoplethysmogram) waveform:

lv_obj_t *chart = lv_chart_create(lv_scr_act());
lv_chart_set_type(chart, LV_CHART_TYPE_LINE);
lv_chart_set_point_count(chart, 90);
lv_chart_set_range(chart, LV_CHART_AXIS_PRIMARY_Y, 0, 2000);

lv_chart_series_t *ser = lv_chart_add_series(chart,
    lv_palette_main(LV_PALETTE_RED), LV_CHART_AXIS_PRIMARY_Y);

Updating the Chart

In the main loop, raw IR values from the MAX30102 are fed into the chart:

long ir = particleSensor.getIR();
lv_chart_set_next_value(chart, ser, ir);
lv_chart_refresh(chart);

BPM Display

A large label shows the real-time BPM:

lv_label_set_text_fmt(bpm_label, "BPM: %d", bpm);

Expected Result

  • A scrolling red line chart showing the PPG waveform

  • Large BPM reading text (e.g., “BPM: 72”)

  • Status indicator showing whether a finger is detected

  • Place your finger on the MAX30102 sensor to see the waveform and BPM

Note

For best results, keep your finger still and apply gentle, consistent pressure. Avoid bright ambient light on the sensor.
